finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Attacker-controlled data in field1 or field2 could lead to format string injection.
finding.assumptions: The printf statement is vulnerable to format string attacks if field1 or field2 contain attacker-controlled data in a format string format.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the received packet size is larger than 4096 bytes, it will overflow the packet buffer.
finding.assumptions: The packet buffer is fixed-size and there is no check on the received packet size to ensure it does not exceed the buffer size.

finding.title: Use of SOCK_RAW Socket
finding.trigger: Using SOCK_RAW allows receiving and sending raw packets, which could lead to network manipulation or injection.
finding.assumptions: The raw socket is used to receive packets without any filtering or validation, which could lead to security issues.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
finding.trigger: If field1 or field2 contain attacker-controlled data, it could lead to XSS if the output is used in a web page.
finding.assumptions: The printf statement is used to output data to the console, but if the output is used in a web page, it could lead to XSS.
